title: Quarterly runway & hypothesis roadmap for Private/VPC feature experimentation
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket scopes a hypothesis-driven quarterly roadmap for private/VPC/on-prem features that need rapid validation before wide rollout. Instead of a single monolithic wave, we will run multiple short, measurable pilot lanes (1–3 weeks each) to validate key assumptions that map to top-level OKRs: reliability under isolation, predictable throughput, and upgrade ergonomics for customer-managed networks.

Why this work now:
- Several enterprise prospects request private deployment SLAs tied to explicit performance guarantees; we need validated guardrails to inform Dedicated/Private packaging and pricing.
- Current roadmap items are high-cost to fully implement without early signal (e.g., private autoscaler tuning, non-standard KMS integration).
- Running small experiments reduces risk and surfaces unexpected network/ops constraints earlier.

Scope and approach:
1) Build a hypothesis bank covering five riskiest assumptions (network egress patterns, KV cache priming in isolated clusters, autoscaler latency under warm/cold starts, KMS round-trip latency, upgrade rollback speed). Each hypothesis is paired with a single success metric and an instrumentation plan.
2) Define 3 pilot lanes: "LANE-CORE" (runtime perf under isolation), "LANE-SEC" (KMS / audit & RBAC flows), "LANE-OPS" (upgrade and rollback timing). Each lane is scoped to a minimal experimentable surface that engineering can implement in ~2 sprints.
3) For each lane, publish an experiment doc (Confluence) with success metrics, dashboards (Grafana links), quick rollback steps, and a test customer cohort (internal + 2 lighthouse customers).
4) Synthesize results into decision gates that inform shipping sequence and OKR outcomes.

Metrics / OKR mapping:
- Objective: Reduce Private deployment TTF (time-to-first-serve) variance by 30% (OKR-Runtime-1). Metric: 95th percentile cold-start latency across pilot lanes.
- Objective: Prevent 90% of customer-visible audit errors on KMS integrations (OKR-Security-2). Metric: KMS end-to-end success rate.
- Objective: Reduce private-upgrade failure windows by 50% (OKR-OPS-3). Metric: Mean time to rollback during staged upgrades.

Deliverables:
- Hypothesis bank (Confluence): /confluence.redwood/private-experiments/2026-q2/hypothesis-bank
- Three pilot lane experiment specs (Confluence) and corresponding Figma playbooks for runbook visuals: Figma file: Private-Experiment-Playbooks (v1)
- Instrumentation dashboards: Grafana panels + alert rules (links in lane docs)
- Post-experiment decision summary with recommended implementation sequencing and OKR updates

Tradeoffs and implementation notes:
- We prioritize short, measurable wins over feature-complete implementations. Tradeoff: pilot lanes may not surface long-tail integration issues but give faster confidence on high-risk assumptions.
- Avoid heavy instrumentation that would distort customer traffic; use synthetic/load probes plus a small number of internal customers.
- Some experiments require ephemeral KMS keys and additional security controls; security needs to sign off before any external customer involvement.

- Design: Priya Iyer (runbook visuals)

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Hypothesis bank created with success metrics and instrumentation plan
Three pilot lane specs published with Grafana dashboards and clear rollback steps
At least 2 internal or lighthouse customers enrolled across lanes
Post-experiment decision memo delivered with explicit go/no-go for full implementation
Security review completed for KMS & audit flows (signed by Omar Gupta)
